Hey Sam — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call so we can move to a short technical pilot: 

Summary of needs we heard:
- Real-time chat generation with sub-200ms token latency SLO for search-assist flows
- Hybrid retrieval: dense embeddings + lightweight lexical filters
- Structured output for agent actions (tool calling) and a reranker for top-k responses
- Tight prompt governance: versioning, injection mitigations, and red-team testing cadence

Proposed next steps (high-level):
1) Technical touchpoint: Dev technical deep-dive to align on SDK, auth, and routing policies (Dev Patel to lead)
2) Pilot scope: 3-week pilot (ingest sample docs, embeddings + reranker, sample prompts)
3) Deliverables: SDK quickstart, sample structured output schema, prompt templates v1, mutual action plan

Items I'm attaching: architecture diagram, SDK quickstart doc, and a first draft of prompt templates (mock_prompt_templates_v1.json).

Can we confirm:
- A 60-90min technical session next week (propose Tue 2026-07-14 10:00 PT)?
- Pilot stakeholders (engineering, infra, security)?

Thanks — I'll loop Neha for timeline/contracting and Dev for the technical session plan.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (technical follow-up)

Thanks Marissa + Sam — quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive so we can hit the ground running:

1) SDK / quickstart- We have official SDKs for Python/Node (pip/npm packages). Quickstart covers auth, streaming, and structured output examples. Will bring a sample repo to the session. See attached redwood_sdk_quickstart.md.

2) Auth options- Short-term: API key with scoped permissions and IP allowlist for pilot.
- Production: recommend OIDC + short-lived tokens (Token Exchange + KMS for key rotation). We can support mutual TLS for VPC/private if needed.

3) Routing & fallbacks- Policy-driven routing: low-latency route to hosted Redwoods (GPU-backed) for interactive flows; fallback to cost-tier model with lower throughput during spikes. We can map routes by API key or tenant id.

4) Embeddings + reranker- Suggested approach: dense-embedding index (512-d) using our embeddings endpoint + approximate k-NN store. Reranker: light-weight cross-encoder hosted on dedicated capacity to rerank top-10 candidates. This balances recall and latency.

5) Structured output & tool-calling- We'll propose a JSON-schema for agent actions (action_type, args, confidence). Use schema validation on the service layer; runtime guardrails in the SDK to reject non-conformant outputs.

6) Prompt governance (initial thoughts)- Version prompts in a Git repo (each template has metadata: id, version, changelog).
- CI: automated prompt tests (sanity checks + red-team test cases) on PRs; block merges if regressions.
- Injection mitigations: input sanitization, system prompt hardening, and strict separation of user content vs. system instructions.

I'll prepare a 40-minute demo+30-minute Q&A for Tue 2026-07-14. If that time works, I’ll send a calendar invite and a short pre-read with sample code snippets.

- Dev

- Latency / batching: for our search-assist use case we expect many short prompts (user + small context). How does batching affect 95th p99 latency? Can you share typical token-per-request tradeoffs?
- Structured output schema: can you share the example JSON-schema you mentioned? We need to validate it against our orchestration layer before the pilot.
- Prompt injection: we run some user-generated content that could try to influence the model. What concrete mitigations do you recommend for the pilot (beyond input sanitization)?

2) concrete JSON-schema for structured output (for your orchestration validation)
3) mock_prompt_templates_v1.json (versioned; PR-based workflow recommended)
4) short red-team checklist and example injection cases

Sam — on prompt injection mitigations specifically:
- Keep system prompts sealed (not editable by end users).
- Use a layered approach: sanitize user input, canonicalize context, and prepend a hardened system prompt with explicit instructions and non-conflicting constraints.
- Runtime validators: if the model produces actions, validate against JSON-schema and reject/flag unexpected fields.
- Red-team cadence: initial red-team during pilot (week 2) then monthly-every-quarter depending on exposure.
